subject: Dedicated pool turnup — EU sizing, burst guardrails & netops checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@praxoshealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@praxoshealth.com>, Julien Moreau <julien.moreau@eurocloud-consulting.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Redwood dedicated onboarding — EU pool sizing question

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with a Dedicated (reserved) pool for our EU production traffic. Before the intake call tomorrow we want to confirm a few items so we can budget and line up our NetOps team: 

- Target steady-state throughput: ~120 req/s for chat-generation (avg 32 tokens per response) during work hours (08:00–18:00 CET).
- Expected peak: 700 req/s during brief daily batch windows (10–12 CET) for document ingestion and reranking.
- SLO: 95th percentile latency < 200ms for interactive paths.

Can Redwood provide an initial sizing recommendation (GPU types + pool count) and a recommended burst/autoscale policy we should expect for PX-4891? Also, what networking prerequisites should our NetOps team have ready (VPC peering, ingress IPs, firewall rules, KMS)?

I've attached our intake spreadsheet — sorry for the rough formatting. Priya will join the call to walk through compliance and data residency constraints.

Appreciate your help,

— Liam
CTO, Praxos Health
liam.oneill@praxoshealth.com
+44 7700 900111

Attachments: praxos-dedicated-intake-form.xlsx
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@praxoshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Julien Moreau <julien.moreau@eurocloud-consulting.com>, Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@praxoshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 16:03:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Redwood dedicated onboarding — EU pool sizing question

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks — received the intake sheet. Quick, high-level notes ahead of the call:

- Sizing: based on 95th token-rate and your steady/peak numbers, recommended starting config is 4x A10-class GPUs for steady traffic with 2x spare capacity for burst headroom. That maps to an initial pool of 6 GPUs; we can propose 2x warm standby nodes for faster warm-up.
- Autoscaling/Burst: configure a conservative autoscale policy with:
  * min_instances: 4
  * target_cpu_utilization: 60%
  * burst_capacity: allow +66% (2 additional GPUs) for short windows (max 20 minutes)
  * warmup_strategy: keep KV-cache-preserving warm-standby when possible to avoid cold-cache penalties
- Latency: to meet 95p < 200ms we'll recommend the A10-class kernel profile and a tokenizer batching cap of 64 tokens/request; if latency slips under load, we propose a vertical bump to A100-class.
- Networking: Redwood needs:
  * VPC peering or private IP connectivity to our EU control plane
  * outbound rules allowing 3 specific egress IPs (we'll provide)
  * TLS mutual-auth for private deployments and a KMS ARN for key wrapping (if you bring your own KMS)

I attached a short NetOps checklist and a link to the EU-region setup guide. For tomorrow's call (10:30 CET) we'll run through these and create an action log with owners.

Quick asks for the call: can Priya confirm data residency constraints (are ephemeral logs allowed in EU multi-az?) and can Julien confirm his timeline for provisioning any cloud accounts/network tickets?

See you on the call,

— Sofia
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-eu-networking-checklist.txt, redwood-dedicated-setup-guide.pdf
From: Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@praxoshealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@praxoshealth.com>, Julien Moreau <julien.moreau@eurocloud-consulting.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 10:50:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Redwood dedicated onboarding — EU pool sizing question

Thanks Sofia — a couple quick clarifications from our side before the action log: 

- Data residency: production customer data must remain in the EU region and any logs containing PII must be quarantined to our tenant. Ephemeral inference KV-cache is okay as long as it does not persist to a globally replicated store.
- Procurement timeline: procurement needs a clear estimate of monthly base capacity + burst delta so finance can finalize the reserved capacity SKU. Can you provide a conservative monthly cost delta for the recommended 6->8 GPU scenario?

Also, NetOps will need the explicit egress IPs and peering steps — Julien will coordinate the cloud account ticketing and expects ~5 business days to get peering approved.

Priya Ramanathan
Head of Ops, Praxos Health
priya.r@praxoshealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Ramanathan <priya.r@praxoshealth.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@praxoshealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 16:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Redwood dedicated onboarding — EU pool sizing question

Hi Priya / Liam,

Following our intake call and the NetOps checklist completion, here's the agreed implementation plan and open owners (action log):

1) Capacity and cost
   - Start: 6x A10-class GPUs (4 active, 2 warm-standby)
   - Burst policy: +2 GPUs (66%) available for bursts up to 20 minutes; autoscale cooldown 5 mins
   - Estimated monthly cost delta (base + expected burst util): €22,400/month (breakdown attached). Please note reserved SKU pricing will drop this by ~18% once procurement signs the annual commit.
   Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood pricing) — deliver detailed quote by Tue 2028-07-16.

2) Networking & Security
   - Redwood will provide 3 egress IPs and a peering playbook by EOD Mon 2028-07-15.
   - If Praxos brings their own KMS, provide KMS ARN; otherwise we can manage keys under SOC2 controls.
   Owner: Marissa Cole (Redwood netops).

3) Rollout & testing
   - Week 1: Provision pool in eu-west-1, smoke tests (latency/throughput), KV-cache warmup scripts.
   - Week 2: Canary traffic (10% production) for 48 hours, monitoring/alerts validated.
   Owner: Sofia Ivanova (CS lead) + Praxos NetOps.

4) Compliance & data residency
   - Logs: configure PII filters and local retention per Praxos policy.
   Owner: Priya Ramanathan (Praxos) + Redwood security.

Attachments: cost-breakdown-eu-a10-6x.csv (will be uploaded to shared Drive).

Next steps: Ben to attach the quote and Marissa will drop the peering playbook link. We'll keep the Drive folder updated with final SOW artifacts. If anything here is incorrect or missing, flag it and we'll update the action log.

Thanks all — excited to get this moving.

— Ben Carter
Director, Dedicated Solutions (Redwood Inference)
ben_carter@redwood.ai
